_comment: Two numerals, and nothing else in this project is generated. The sheet's eleven hundred characters are typed by render_page.py because no local model sets that much text without inventing some of it; two digits against a reference of two digits is the other side of that line, and the reference is the act's own pencilled 10. Run tools/pencil_layer.py cut first -- it writes input/pencil_corner.png (where the number goes, cut from the finished plate) and input/pencil_ref.png (the hand to copy). Then tools/pencil_layer.py lift takes the difference and hands render_page.py a pigment layer with an alpha, so the mark ends up on the sheet's real grain rather than on the model's idea of paper.
_pencil: The act's mark is a blue copying pencil, not the violet render_page.PENCIL draws: measured over the 815 pixels where blue runs 18 levels over red, it is (147,171,180) and (122,148,160) through the core, and it stands 3.83% of the sheet high -- 392 px on a 10240 sheet, which is the `size` for the pencil directive.
_verify: Node names are the stock Qwen-Image-Edit set; load this in the UI once before trusting it in a batch. The two settings that matter: cfg 1.0 and 4 steps, because the Lightning LoRA is a 4-step distillation and anything above cfg 1 with it comes back scorched.
_reroll: Change `seed`. Judge on the lift, not on the picture: pencil_layer.py prints what fraction of the crop changed, and a run that repaints the paper as well as writing on it shows up there as a number over 8% while looking fine to the eye.

positive._comment: The prompt describes the medium, not the look: indelible pencil is a pigment that dissolves where the hand pressed damp, which is why the act's 10 has a violet halo round a near-black core. Ask for the halo and the break and the model draws a mark; ask for 'handwritten number' and it draws a font.

inputs.prompt: Write the number 67 on the blank paper in image1, in the same blue copying pencil and the same hand as the number in image2: the same pale blue-grey pigment, soft and slightly translucent, laid down in a broad blunt stroke that breaks over the grain of the paper and is not continuous. The same pressure, the same slight rightward slant, the same size. Change nothing else: the paper, its tone, its creases and its grain stay exactly as they are.
printed digits, typeface, ballpoint, felt tip, clean even stroke, outline, drop shadow, new paper texture, redrawn background
